A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core algorithms and experiments. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and visual results, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original text-to-3D experiments, image-editing comparisons, a user study and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds reconstruction measurements, editing-variant comparisons and further qualitative 3D comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix K add an inference variant that inserts the learned iRFDS noise at an intermediate generation point, reported as 10% of the trajectory, instead of using it as the initial noise. The underlying RFDS, iRFDS and RFDS-Rev objectives and algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 adds an explicit reconstruction scenario using unchanged image content and captions, whereas v3 evaluates inversion through subsequent editing. This limited extension uses the same image dataset; T3Bench and the 15-image editing set are retained. The added 3DGS experiments change model configuration rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix O and Figure 19 substantially broaden the 3D comparator set beyond the existing SDS/VSD comparisons by adding LucidDreamer, DreamCraft3D and GaussianDreamer. These methods participate in a four-prompt qualitative comparison, although they are not added to the quantitative T3Bench table. Existing editing and benchmark comparators remain.

E3.justification: The user study changes from a general preference question to separate semantic-correspondence and unrelated-region-consistency questions, confirmed by the survey screenshots. v4 also introduces PSNR reconstruction evaluation and qualitative experiments using a 3DGS backbone. Existing T3Bench settings, training budgets and editing-set size remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 12 adds a comparison of initial versus intermediate noise insertion, examining background and color preservation, and Figure 13 adds reconstruction diagnostics. Figure 7 also adds RFDS-Rev without the Jacobian to the existing Jacobian comparison. Earlier step-count, guidance-scale and RFDS-VSD ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The revised preference percentages and new PSNR values do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 and Table 2's CLIP scores are unchanged. The former aggregate preference results are replaced by criterion-specific results: iRFDS/InstaFlow's 45.3% becomes 43.6% semantic preference and 33.4% consistency preference, which are different judgments rather than directly comparable performance changes. v4 newly reports reconstruction PSNR of 28.52 for baseline iRFDS, 28.96 with intermediate insertion and 28.81 for null-inversion, alongside additional qualitative and wall-clock results.

T1.justification: New Appendix B derives a relationship between Euler sampling updates and the RFDS residual through Equations 11–14, motivating noise reversal through fixed versus resampled noise. This is a limited new mathematical derivation; the original loss derivations, Reflow assumption and diffusion/SDS equivalence argument are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: rectified-flow models can serve as priors, RFDS/RFDS-Rev outperform SDS/VSD in text-to-3D generation, and iRFDS supports competitive inversion and editing. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds an Euler-based explanation of noise reversal, including why one fixed noise cannot serve every rendered 3D view. It also discusses the editing-versus-consistency balance of intermediate insertion and interprets the new examples as evidence of NeRF/3DGS applicability. Existing multi-face, CFG-mismatch and inherited-bias limitations remain; broader impacts are relocated.

D1.justification: v4 adds RFDS runtime estimates of approximately 20 minutes with InstaFlow and 40 minutes with SD3, supplements the diffusion-method timing comparison, and documents the intermediate insertion point and revised survey questions. Previously reported hardware, optimization settings, noise regularization and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to Prompt-to-Prompt, LucidDreamer, DreamCraft3D, GaussianDreamer and Yang et al.'s noise-recalibration work, while trimming general background citations such as Stable Video Diffusion and Brock's GAN paper. The central positioning as an early study of rectified-flow priors remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction is condensed and several explanatory paragraphs are rewritten. Broader impacts move into Appendix A, new appendix subsections are inserted, and acknowledgements and the ICLR publication header are added. Most method and experimental prose retains its previous organization and wording.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures 12, 13 and 19, expands Figure 7, splits Table 2's preference reporting into two rows, and replaces the survey screenshot with two question panels. Several existing displays move or shrink; v3's Figures 12–15 are retained as v4's Figures 14–17 rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The separated editing criteria and new reconstruction comparisons provide useful evidence about fidelity that v3's aggregate preference results did not isolate. The Euler derivation and additional 3D comparators also strengthen explanation and contextual evaluation. These gains are limited: the main benchmark results are unchanged, the new 3D comparison is qualitative, and participant counts and uncertainty remain unreported.
